name: High-grade dysplasia in patients with Barrett esophagus

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological criteria for high-grade dysplasia in Barrett esophagus

criteria.description: Marked cytologic atypia including nuclear enlargement, hyperchromasia, and pleomorphism
Complex glandular architectural distortion with gland crowding and cribriform patterns
Increased mitotic activity including abnormal mitoses in the epithelium
No evidence of invasive adenocarcinoma on biopsy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of marked cytologic atypia and architectural glandular distortion without evidence of invasive carcinoma
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires expert gastrointestinal pathology review due to overlap with low-grade dysplasia and carcinoma.

laboratory: Iron deficiency anemia on CBC due to chronic occult bleeding
Elevated inflammatory markers may be present but nonspecific
imaging: Endoscopic visualization of Barrett mucosa with nodularity or ulceration
Endoscopic ultrasound showing mucosal thickening without invasion
genetic: p53 mutations frequently detected in dysplastic Barrett epithelium
Loss of heterozygosity at 9p21 and 17p loci
other: Histopathology demonstrating marked cytologic and architectural atypia

distinguishingFeatures: Lower risk of progression to adenocarcinoma
More pronounced clinical symptoms including severe dysphagia and weight loss

redFlags: Endoscopic evidence of mucosal nodularity or ulceration
references: American Gastroenterological Association Medical Position Statement on the Management of Barrett's Esophagus
Shaheen NJ, et al. ACG Clinical Guideline: Diagnosis and Management of Barrett's Esophagus. Am J Gastroenterol. 2016.
Odze RD. Diagnosis and grading of dysplasia in Barrett's esophagus. J Clin Pathol. 2006.
